_note: HAND-AUTHORED. The prerequisite spine of Grade 6. Nothing else in this repo encodes which standard has to be understood BEFORE another one can be, so causal tracing ('they are not failing X, they are failing Y underneath it') is impossible without this file. Node ids use the NORMALIZED form that data/asset-concept-map.json uses (cluster letter dropped: 6.AT.A.3.a -> 6.AT.3a), so the graph joins directly to assets. Validated as a DAG by tools/validate-nervous-system.mjs.

strengths.core: The dependent standard is not learnable without this one. Trace here first.
strengths.supporting: Makes the dependent standard much easier; a gap here shows up as slowness and hint use, not as total failure.
strengths.fluency: A computational prerequisite. A gap here looks like careless arithmetic inside otherwise-correct reasoning.

edges.why: A unit rate is a ratio re-expressed per one. Without a stable ratio concept, 'per one' is just an unmotivated division.
Finding a unit rate is a division. Shaky multi-digit division shows up as wrong unit rates that are reasoned correctly.
Rate reasoning in context is unit-rate thinking applied to a situation.
Equivalent-ratio tables are the organized form of the rate reasoning students do informally first.
Plotting the table on the coordinate plane requires placing ordered pairs.
Unit conversion is a rate applied as a multiplier.
Percent is a rate per 100. Students who cannot reason with rates cannot reason with percents.
Percent work is decimal work. Place-value slips here read as percent misconceptions but are not.
The decimal algorithms are the whole-number algorithms with place value tracked.
Common factors are what make a fraction quotient simplifiable and interpretable.
Generating equivalent expressions by factoring IS the distributive property over a common factor.
Volume with fractional edge lengths is fraction multiplication in three dimensions.
Area of triangles and composed figures requires confident decimal and fraction arithmetic.
Surface area from a net is the sum of the face areas; the area work has to be automatic first.
Polygons drawn in the plane are still polygons: the area and side-length reasoning transfers.
Drawing polygons in the coordinate plane depends on four-quadrant plotting and distance.
Negative numbers have to mean something in context before they can be located on a line.
Placement on the plane generalizes placement on the line.
Opposites are a statement about symmetric position on the number line.
Reflections across axes are sign changes on an already-understood ordered pair.
Ordering rational numbers is reading position on the number line.
Interpreting an inequality statement presumes the ordering it asserts.
Explaining an ordering in context is interpretation plus justification.
Absolute value is distance from zero on the line students have just learned to order.
Four-quadrant problem solving needs signed ordered pairs to be secure.
Distance between points on a shared line is an absolute-value idea.
Evaluating expressions requires exponent notation to already be readable.
Writing an expression from words presumes knowing what an expression is.
Naming terms, factors and coefficients is structural reading of an expression.
Substituting a value presumes the letter-for-number idea.
Equivalence is argued over terms and factors; you cannot rewrite structure you cannot name.
Checking equivalence by substitution is the students' first proof of equivalence.
Solving is finding the value that makes two expressions equivalent.
An inequality is the same truth question with a range of answers instead of one.
Dependent/independent relationships are equations read as a rule.
The ratio table is the first table of a dependent relationship students ever build.
Graphing the relationship requires the coordinate plane.
You cannot talk about a distribution until you accept that the question anticipates variability.
Center and spread only mean something against the shape of a distribution.
The mean is a decimal division. Averaging errors are often arithmetic errors.
A dot plot, histogram or box plot is a picture of the distribution.
Every one of these displays is built on a number line.
Summarizing a data set in context requires the summary measures to exist first.
Summary claims are read off the display.
Reporting n is the first move of a full summary.
Naming the attribute and its units is the second move of a full summary.
Reporting center and variability is the third move of a full summary.
Choosing WHICH measure fits the shape is the judgement that comes after computing both.

tagStandards._note: Which standard a live misconception tag is diagnostic OF. This is the join that turns a telemetry tag into a node on the map. Ordered most-diagnostic first.
